ruling.explanation: The rule 'making-an-attack > ranged-attacks > ranged-attacks-in-close-combat' states that you have disadvantage on a ranged attack if you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature who can see you and isn't incapacitated. The fact from the question is that the enemy is standing right next to you (within 5 feet). Therefore, you have disadvantage.

The rule 'making-an-attack > melee-attacks > two-weapon-fighting' states that when you take the Attack action and attack with a light melee weapon in one hand, you can use a bonus action to attack with a different light melee weapon in the other hand. The rule 'weapon-properties > thrown' states that if a weapon has the thrown property, you can throw it to make a ranged attack instead of making a melee attack. A handaxe is a light melee weapon with the thrown property. Therefore, when attacking with one handaxe, the bonus action attack with the other handaxe can be made as a throw.

The rule for Sneak Attack states you deal extra damage if you have advantage on the attack roll OR if another enemy is within 5 feet of the target (and other conditions are met). The question asks about a rogue with advantage attacking with a longsword. A longsword does not have the finesse property, so normally you cannot add Dexterity to the attack roll. However, the rule explicitly grants Sneak Attack if you 'have advantage on the attack roll', regardless of weapon type or Dexterity modifier usage. The text allows no other reading here; having advantage is a sufficient condition listed in the first paragraph of the Sneak Attack entry.

The rule states you do not need advantage for Sneak Attack if another enemy is within 5 feet of the target and that enemy isn't incapacitated. The fact from the question is that an orc (an enemy) is standing next to the goblin (the target). Therefore, the condition for Sneak Attack without advantage is met.

The rule for Martial Arts states that monk weapons are 'shortswords and any simple melee weapons that don't have the two-handed or heavy property.' A greatclub is a simple melee weapon, but it has the 'heavy' property. Therefore, it does not meet the criteria to be considered a monk weapon under this feature.

The rule for 'class-features > fighter > fighting-style-great-weapon-fighting' states that when you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack with a melee weapon wielded with two hands, you can reroll the die. The fact from the question is that the character is a Fighter wielding a longsword (which has the 'Versatile' property) in both hands. Since the longsword allows two-handed use and the character has the Great Weapon Fighting style, the condition to reroll damage dice on 1s or 2s is met.

The rule 'class-features > fighter > action-surge' states that at 2nd level, a Fighter can take one additional action on top of their regular action. Therefore, the condition of using a 'ranged weapon' for the sneak attack is met when throwing a handaxe.
